docs.title: e8358a – Agilent / Keysight E8358A PNA network analyzer (E8356A / E8357A too)
docs.text:
Vector network analyzer

property value driver name e8358a module easymeasure.drivers.e8358a interfaces GPIB (gpib), USB-TMC (usb), VISA LAN (tcpip), TCP socket (tcp), serial (serial), other VISA (other), simulated bus (sim) recognised by *IDN? E8356A, E8357A, E8358A suggested addresses SIM::e8358a (built-in emulator) shared port by default no

Agilent (now Keysight) PNA series vector network analyzers: the E8358A (300 kHz – 9 GHz), and the E8356A (3 GHz) and E8357A (6 GHz), which use the same commands. Connect over LAN (TCPIP0::<ip>::inst0::INSTR, or the socket TCPIP0::<ip>::5025::SOCKET) or GPIB.

  • Traces: S11, S21, S12, S22 as log magnitude (dB), with …_phase (degrees) and …_re / …_im (the complex value). Each is a whole sweep; its x axis is frequencies (Hz), which the plots and the data files use.
  • Source: power (dBm) is an ordinary channel: alias it with limits and sweep it, for a power dependence.
  • Settings: f_start, f_stop, f_center, f_span, points (1 – 16001), if_bandwidth (the analyzer's list, 1 Hz – 40 kHz), sweep_type (LIN / LOG), averaging and average_count, output (RF on / off) and correction (the channel's calibration, made on the analyzer).
  • Actions: single_sweep, continuous (free run, for the front panel), delete_traces and preset (below).

Measurements. The driver creates a measurement on channel 1 of the analyzer (EM_S21, …) the first time an S-parameter is read, and shows it in window 1. The analyzer's other measurements are left alone. With the option parameters, e.g. "S21,S11", they are created when connecting, so that the first sweep already measures them all. Option channel uses another channel of the analyzer.

One sweep per point. Reading a trace starts a single sweep of all measurements and waits for it to end. The other traces of that sweep (S21_phase, S11 …) are read from the same sweep: recording S21 and S21_phase at a point costs one sweep. With averaging on, a reading is always a complete, fresh average of average_count sweeps. The sweep time is about points / IF bandwidth per direction; S12 or S22 together with S11 or S21 adds the reverse sweep. Afterwards the analyzer holds the last sweep on its screen; continuous lets it sweep freely again.

Starting clean: delete_traces. The analyzer sweeps every measurement on the channel, also ones made at its front panel and ones read earlier: a leftover S12 or S22 adds the reverse sweep and roughly doubles the time of every sweep. delete_traces deletes every measurement on the analyzer and leaves every setting as it is; afterwards only what is read is measured. Make it the first pre-sweep constant of a sweep (channel vna.delete_traces, no value):

"pre": {"constants": [{"channel": "vna.delete_traces"},
                      {"channel": "vna.if_bandwidth", "value": 1000}]}

preset is the analyzer's factory preset (SYSTem:FPReset): every setting goes back to its factory default - a wide span, 201 points, 35 kHz IF bandwidth, 0 dBm with RF on, no averaging, correction off (check the values on your analyzer: options and firmware change them) - and every measurement and window is deleted. Calibrations saved on the analyzer stay, but are no longer applied. Mind the power: a device that wants −60 dBm gets 0 dBm. To start clean but keep the settings, use delete_traces.

A sweep that has not ended after three times the expected time plus sweep_timeout (30 s) is an error. A setting the analyzer refuses (out of range, correction without a calibration …) raises with the analyzer's own message.

SIM::e8358a is an emulator: a hanger resonator at 5 GHz behind a lossy cable, with noise that falls with power, IF bandwidth and averaging.

docs.title: hp34401a – HP/Agilent 34401A 6.5 digit multimeter (V, I, R; DC and AC)
docs.text:
Digital multimeter

property value driver name hp34401a module easymeasure.drivers.hp34401a interfaces GPIB (gpib), serial (serial), TCP socket (tcp), simulated bus (sim) recognised by *IDN? 34401 suggested addresses SIM::hp34401a (built-in emulator) shared port by default no

HP / Agilent / Keysight 34401A 6½-digit multimeter.

The reading channel is named after the mode: Vdc, Vac, Idc, Iac, R2w or R4w. An alias on dmm.Vdc therefore cannot record a current by mistake after somebody switched the meter to Idc. It reports an error until the mode is back.

  • Settings: range (or auto), nplc, autozero (DC and resistance), and ac_filter (AC).
  • Timeouts: reading timeouts follow the NPLC and the AC filter.
  • Overload: 9.9E37 reads as ±inf.

It is reachable over GPIB and RS-232. Several 34401As can share a Prologix adapter: use the options shared and gpib_addr.

docs.title: Add it

docs.title: hp4145 – HP 4145A/B (or 4155/4156 in 4145 syntax) parameter analyzer, user mode
docs.text:
Semiconductor parameter analyzer

property value driver name hp4145 module easymeasure.drivers.hp4145 interfaces GPIB (gpib), serial (serial), TCP socket (tcp), simulated bus (sim) suggested addresses SIM::hp4145 (built-in emulator) shared port by default no

HP 4145A/B semiconductor parameter analyzer, and the HP 4155/4156 in 4145 syntax.

The analyzer is put into HP-IB user mode (US). Every SMU is forced (DV / DI) and measured (TV / TI) point by point, so it works like four source-measure units, with the same mode<n> logic and adaptive compliance as the Keithley 2400.

  • Per SMU 1…4: voltage<n>, current<n>, mode<n>, Icompliance<n> / Vcompliance<n>, output<n> and range<n>.
  • Voltage sources vs1, vs2 and voltage monitors vm1, vm2.
  • integration: short / medium / long.

Settings. User mode has no setting queries, so settings are remembered by the driver. A value written while output<n> is OFF is applied when it is switched ON; this needs a compliance first.

Output envelope. The envelope is checked before anything is sent:

current voltage 100 mA ≤ 20 V 50 mA ≤ 40 V 20 mA ≤ 100 V

Reconnect. A reconnect does not touch the outputs; they then read OFF until set again.

4155 / 4156. A 4155/4156 is switched into its 4145 syntax command mode automatically when it is in SCPI mode (:SYST:LANG COMP) or FLEX mode (:PAGE first), checked with CMD?. The option force_4145_syntax = false leaves the mode alone.

Not yet confirmed from the manual text:

  • the mode switch commands;
  • the VS/VM channel numbers (5, 6) and DS <ch>;
  • the exact TV/TI reply layout. The parser accepts the usual variants: status character first and number last; overflow reads as ±inf, oscillation as NaN.

docs.title: keithley2400 – Keithley 2400 SourceMeter (voltage or current source, measure the other)
docs.text:
Source-measure unit

property value driver name keithley2400 module easymeasure.drivers.keithley2400 interfaces GPIB (gpib), serial (serial), TCP socket (tcp), simulated bus (sim) recognised by *IDN? KEITHLEY suggested addresses SIM::keithley2400 (built-in emulator) shared port by default no

Keithley 2400-series SourceMeter (2400, 2401, 2410, 2420, 2425, 2430, 2440): one source-measure unit.

Modes. In Voltage mode, voltage is the source (read/write) and current is measured (read-only); the compliance is the current limit Icompliance in A. In Current mode it is the other way round, with Vcompliance in V. The front ends follow the switch at once.

  • Changing the mode requires the output to be OFF. The driver refuses otherwise, rather than switching under load.
  • The measured quantity reads NaN while the output is off, because nothing is measured.

sense selects 2- or 4-wire sensing, terminals front or rear, and nplc the integration time.

A typical I–V curve in current mode, with Isrc → smu.current and Vmeas → smu.voltage:

{"name": "iv", "dimensions": [{"points": 101,
   "sweep": [{"channel": "Isrc", "start": 0, "stop": 1e-6}], "record": ["Vmeas"]}],
 "pre":  {"constants": [{"channel": "smu.mode", "value": "Current"},
                        {"channel": "smu.Vcompliance", "value": 2},
                        {"channel": "smu.output", "value": "ON"}]},
 "post": {"constants": [{"channel": "Isrc", "value": 0}, {"channel": "smu.output", "value": "OFF"}]}}

Options: verify_writes reads every source value back, which is worth it on RS-232. check_errors reads the error queue after every setting, so a refused value raises the instrument's own message.

docs.text:
Source-measure unit

property value driver name keysight_b2901 module easymeasure.drivers.keysight_b2901 interfaces GPIB (gpib), USB-TMC (usb), VISA LAN (tcpip), TCP socket (tcp), serial (serial), other VISA (other), simulated bus (sim) recognised by *IDN? B29 suggested addresses SIM::keysight_b2901 (built-in emulator) shared port by default no

Keysight B2901A/B2911A (and B2961) precision source/measure unit, one output. It works like the Keithley 2400: mode Voltage / Current, the measured quantity read-only, Icompliance ↔ Vcompliance. In addition:

  • low: the low terminal grounded or floating;
  • NPLC up to 100.

The measured quantity reads NaN while the output is off. The B2900 would otherwise switch its output on by itself for a measurement. The mode can only be changed with the output off.

Reachable over GPIB, USB-TMC, LAN (VISA or a raw socket on port 5025) and serial.

docs.title: ni6211 – NI USB-6211 DAQ: 16 AI, 2 AO, 4 DI, 4 DO, 2 counters (NI-DAQmx)
docs.text:
Multifunction DAQ

property value driver name ni6211 module easymeasure.drivers.ni6211 interfaces NI-DAQmx (daq) recognised by *IDN? USB-621 suggested addresses DAQ::SIM (built-in emulation) shared port by default no

NI USB-6211 multifunction DAQ, through NI-DAQmx. It needs NI's NI-DAQmx driver runtime; the nidaqmx Python package comes with easyMeasure.

Address: DAQ::Dev1, the device name in NI MAX. DAQ::SIM is the built-in emulator, with loop-back wiring: aiK sees aoK.

Channels: ai0…ai15 (ai0…7 in DIFF), the vector ai, ao0, ao1, di0…3, do0…3, ctr0 and ctr1.

Settings: rate, samples, terminal (RSE / NRSE / DIFF) and ai_range.

Readings. Every analog reading is the mean of samples samples at rate per input. It acquires only the inputs it returns:

  • ai3 alone, up to 250 kS/s;
  • the vector ai, all inputs of one scan, which share the 250 kS/s. The option ai_channels, e.g. "0-3", puts fewer inputs in it. A vector reading too fast for its inputs is refused; the single inputs still work.

samples = 1 is a single on-demand conversion, taking well under a millisecond.

(DAQ::SIM is the driver's built-in emulator; use the instrument's real address for hardware.)

docs.title: ni63xx – NI USB-63xx X Series DAQ (USB-6341 … 6366, NI-DAQmx): analog / digital channels follow the model
docs.text:
Multifunction DAQ (X Series)

property value driver name ni63xx module easymeasure.drivers.ni63xx interfaces NI-DAQmx (daq) recognised by *IDN? USB-6341, USB-6343, USB-6346, USB-6349, USB-6351, USB-6353, USB-6356, USB-6361, USB-6363, USB-6366 suggested addresses DAQ::SIM (built-in emulation) shared port by default no

One driver for the ten NI USB X Series multifunction DAQs, in their BNC, screw terminal, mass termination and OEM variants, through NI-DAQmx (NI's runtime required).

model is a configuration channel, and also an instrument option, so a setup keeps it. It picks the exact model, and the channel list is rebuilt from NI's specifications for it:

model analog in out port 0 AI ranges AO ranges max rate USB-6341 / 6343 16 / 32 SE (8 / 16 DIFF) 2 / 4 8 / 32 ±0.2…10 V (4) ±10 V 500 kS/s total USB-6351 / 6353 16 / 32 SE (8 / 16 DIFF) 2 / 4 8 / 32 ±0.1…10 V (7) ±10, ±5 V 1.25 MS/s one input, 1 MS/s total USB-6361 / 6363 16 / 32 SE (8 / 16 DIFF) 2 / 4 8 / 32 ±0.1…10 V (7) ±10, ±5 V 2 MS/s one input, 1 MS/s total USB-6346 / 6349 8 / 32 DIFF, simultaneous 2 8 ±1…10 V (4) ±10 V 500 kS/s per input USB-6356 8 DIFF, simultaneous 2 8 ±1…10 V (4) ±10, ±5 V 1.25 MS/s per input USB-6366 8 DIFF, simultaneous 2 8 ±1…10 V (4) ±10, ±5 V 2 MS/s per input

All have 16 PFI lines (pfi0…15 = P1 / P2) and 4 counters.

model = auto takes what the device reports. A model that does not match the device is refused; a device type the table does not know is trusted to be the model you set.

Changing the model. Settings the new model does not support fall back, with a log message: the terminal to RSE or DIFF, the ranges to ±10 V, and the rate lowered to fit.

Inputs. In DIFF the inputs are the pairs aiK / aiK+8, so ai0…7 (and ai16…23 on the 32-input models). Readings work as on the USB-6211: the mean of samples samples, acquiring only the inputs returned. The vector ai shares the aggregate rate.

Digital lines are inputs until written. A written line is an output driving that level until release_digital.

Counters. A counter (ctrK, started by its first reading) uses its default source, PFI 8 / 3 / 0 / 5. That line then refuses to be a digital line.

Emulator. DAQ::SIM emulates the chosen model (auto → USB-6363) with a loop-back: aiK sees aoK, and each digital line is wired to the one half a port away.

docs.title: scpi_generic – Generic SCPI instrument defined by option 'channels'
docs.text:
Any SCPI instrument (configured by options)

property value driver name scpi_generic module easymeasure.drivers.scpi_generic interfaces GPIB (gpib), USB-TMC (usb), VISA LAN (tcpip), TCP socket (tcp), serial (serial), other VISA (other), simulated bus (sim) shared port by default no

A SCPI instrument described entirely by its options, with no driver code. Its channels and actions come from the options channels and actions:

c.call("add_instrument", name="ps", driver="scpi_generic", address="GPIB0::5::INSTR",
       options={
         "idn_contains": "KEITHLEY",
         "init": ["*RST", ":SOUR:FUNC VOLT"],
         "channels": [
           {"name": "V", "access": "rw", "get": ":SOUR:VOLT?",
            "set": ":SOUR:VOLT {value:.6g}", "unit": "V"},
           {"name": "I", "access": "r", "get": ":MEAS:CURR?", "unit": "A", "index": 1},
           {"name": "trace", "access": "r", "get": ":TRAC:DATA?", "shape": [-1]},
           {"name": "output", "access": "rw", "dtype": "str", "get": ":OUTP?",
            "set": ":OUTP {value}", "config": True}],
         "actions": [{"name": "trigger", "command": "*TRG"},
                     {"name": "reset", "command": ["*RST", "*CLS"]}]})
  • index picks one element of a comma-separated reply.
  • Vector channels (shape: [-1]) parse comma-separated replies into arrays.
  • It works with any port type: VISA, serial, TCP.

For anything more than a few channels, the Driver Wizard is more convenient. It writes a real driver file, with an error queue, allowed values, value maps, checks and a try-it step.

docs.title: Python API
docs.text:
Class SCPIGeneric in module easymeasure.drivers.scpi_generic.

Base class for instrument drivers.

Subclasses set CHANNELS (a list of ChannelSpec) and implement either read/write or _read_<channel> / _write_<channel> methods. Inside driver methods use self.resource for I/O - the handle has already opened a transaction on it.

  • Sources: sine_out (amplitude), frequency, phase and aux_out1…4. These are ordinary channels: alias them with limits and ramp rates, and sweep them.
  • Settings: reference (internal / external), sensitivity, time_constant, rolloff, coupling, ground, line_filter, input, reserve, harmonic and sync_filter. Sensitivities and time constants are human-readable ("500 µV", "300 ms").
  • Actions: auto gain, auto phase, auto reserve.

With a current input (input = I), the sensitivities are listed in A, and X / Y / R are in A. frequency is read-only with an external reference.

Xn / Yn are measured on the instrument's displays. On the SR830, CH1 / CH2 are set to X / Y noise on the first read; on the SR850, traces 3 and 4 are used.

Set pre_delay in sweeps to a few time constants.

docs.title: Add it
docs.text:
c.call("add_instrument", name="lockin", driver="sr830", address="SIM::sr830")

(SIM::sr830 is the driver's built-in emulator; use the instrument's real address for hardware.)

Class SR830 in module easymeasure.drivers.sr830.

Base of SCPI drivers: identification, error queue, emulator for SIM::.

Subclasses set IDN_MATCH (any of these substrings must occur in *IDN?, case-insensitively) and EMULATOR (a factory for the SIM:: emulator).

Option gpib_addr (with shared = true): the instrument sits behind a Prologix-style GPIB adapter together with others; ++addr N selects it.

docs.title: yokogawa7651 – Yokogawa 7651 programmable DC voltage / current source
docs.text:
DC voltage / current source

property value driver name yokogawa7651 module easymeasure.drivers.yokogawa7651 interfaces GPIB (gpib), serial (serial), TCP socket (tcp), simulated bus (sim) suggested addresses SIM::yokogawa7651 (built-in emulator) shared port by default no

Yokogawa 7651 programmable DC source. It is a source only, with no measurement. The source channel is named after the mode:

mode channel ranges Voltage voltage 10 mV … 30 V Current current 1 … 100 mA

Ranges. With range = AUTO, the driver picks the smallest range that holds the value. While the output is ON it only ever ranges up, so a sweep coming down does not glitch the output with range changes. A fixed range refuses values beyond 120 % of it.

The compliance is Icompliance in voltage mode and Vcompliance in current mode.

Verified settings. Every setting is executed (E) and read back (OD). An error flag, or a value that did not arrive, raises an error, and a command lost on the bus is retried.
